correctness.rationale: The combination counts in sizes 0 through 4 are 1,35,595,6545,52360. An independently written enumeration (branches/50fab930-c645-49c2-84ee-dd2297700735/reproduce_kg73.py and reproduction.txt, under /workspace) rebuilt the disjointness graph and monotone closure from closed neighborhoods and found 0,0,0,0,840 successful sets, exactly the generated pencil-plus-transversal family. The root is uniquely recoverable as the only point on three selected triples. Completing the three rooted pairs to a Fano design forces the four unrooted lines to be the given transversal and the three choices changing exactly two of its pair selections, since Fano lines meet in one point; this covers every interpair point pair once. Independently, exact cover of all 21 point pairs gave 30 labelled planes and their 840 distinct antiflags, with one preimage per placement. Removing the transversal permits the other seven transversals, only the complement disjoint from it. On removing a pencil line, the two retained lines and transversal have three different pairwise intersections. The old root forces the removed line; each other possible root gives one new pencil line, sharing a point with the removed line. Thus there are 13 jumps and one slide, and the independent graph traversal reproduced 5460 jump edges, distance shells (1,13,39,87,204,320,176) from every vertex, radius and diameter 6, and 420 slide components of order 2. Ground-point permutations act transitively on the pencil/transversal data. The enumeration checks the entire stated domain; no supplied verifier was executed.

value.rationale: This is a natural small odd graph, not an arbitrary labelled instance. The exact family identifies all minimal-budget placements geometrically and makes the effect of constraining moves stark: all placements communicate in at most six unrestricted minimum-preserving jumps, but slides are confined to pairs. The Fano completion gives a structural explanation rather than just an unmotivated count.
